correctness.rationale: Transitivity forbids tangency of distinct members. The ordered pair-incidence projection is therefore a proper submersion; its nonempty image is open and closed in the connected ordered two-point configuration space. A nearby fiber is the regular zero set of an infinitesimal variation, which Martins identifies with an equator or projective hyperplane, and Ehresmann propagation identifies every fiber. Fixing one member and applying isotopy extension gives the standard embedding type.

originality.rationale: The recent Martins preprint gives ambient and parameter-space rigidity plus the local nodal classification, but no arbitrary-pair incidence theorem was found. Searches of the principal earlier Zoll-family papers, external literature, and current SCOPE records found no statement that all distinct members intersect transversely with the stated standard codimension-two topology or that the pair-incidence space fibers over the ordered configuration space.

value.rationale: The theorem globalizes local projective incidence to every pair, including nonlinearly deformed transitive sphere families that cannot be globally straightened. It supplies a reusable configuration-space bundle and gives an exact intersection law for hypersurface Zoll families, including a single transverse circle for every pair of distinct surface-Zoll members in dimension three.
